summary.allegation: The issuer says the cardholder was billed twice for the same purchase by Roastline Coffee Co on 12 April 2025, with two identical charges of GBP 54.00 when only one purchase was made.
summary.to_defend: Visa requires evidence that the two charges relate to two genuinely separate purchases, with separate purchase documentation and distinct timestamps and authorisation codes.

requirements.title: Two separate purchases
requirements.text: Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered).
requirements.finding: The merchant supplied two invoices with different invoice numbers, different order IDs and entirely different baskets: coffee beans on RL-ORDER-44188 and an Aeropress Go kit with filter papers on RL-ORDER-44192. The amounts match at GBP 54.00 only because a GBP 6.00 loyalty discount was applied to the first order.

requirements.title: Each purchase documented
requirements.text: Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates).
requirements.finding: Each purchase event has its own invoice and its own DPD consignment with a separate delivery date, 14 April 2025 on tracking 7711224488 and 15 April 2025 on tracking 7711224501.

requirements.title: Timestamps and auth codes
requirements.text: Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge.
requirements.finding: Both charges carry distinct capture timestamps and distinct authorisation codes, 442189 captured at 08:11:33 on 12 April and 552781 captured at 19:42:18 the same evening; the disputed transaction record shows the morning charge at 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z for GBP 54.00.

alerts.text: The first invoice labels the capture as 12 Apr 2025 08:11:33 BST while the transaction record shows 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z, so the two sources state the same clock time in different zones and differ by one hour; confirm which reading is correct before filing.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

justification: All three requirements are satisfied by two separate invoices with different order IDs, items, deliveries, timestamps and authorisation codes.
rationale:
The issuer alleges a duplicate charge of GBP 54.00 on 12 April 2025 for a single purchase.
The merchant evidences two distinct orders placed the same day, RL-ORDER-44188 at 08:11 for coffee beans and RL-ORDER-44192 at 19:42 for an Aeropress Go kit and filter papers.
The amounts are equal only because a GBP 6.00 loyalty discount reduced the GBP 60.00 first order to GBP 54.00.
Each charge has its own authorisation code, 442189 and 552781, and its own DPD consignment delivered on 14 and 15 April 2025 respectively.
The charges are not duplicates and the chargeback should be represented in full.
